actions.body:
As automated decision systems become more prevalent across societal domains, establishing clear lines of responsibility becomes crucial. Recent work examines ethics-based auditing (EBA) as a soft yet formal governance mechanism. Rather than solving the deep philosophical questions of machine consciousness or moral agency, EBA focuses on structured documentation and intervention points throughout the software development lifecycle. By requiring systematic records and promoting ethical deliberation at critical junctures, these frameworks help organizations verify claims and provide decision-subjects with justified explanations for automated outputs.

Summary
This article examines how structured auditing practices help bridge accountability gaps in automated systems by establishing clear documentation and deliberation points during software development.
actions.lede: Exploring how structured auditing and governance frameworks bridge the gap between automated software outputs and meaningful human accountability.
